subject: Novamed RFI: location-specific hosting dependencies & exceptions

From: Emma Collins <emma.collins@novamed.com>
To: vanessa_ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>, procurement@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-05-12T14:08:00Z
Subject: RFI: location-specific hosting dependencies and exceptions

Hi Vanessa,

Thanks for taking our RFI. We have a set of focused questions around data residency and any hosting dependencies or exceptions that could affect EU-only workloads. High level: Novamed requires processing and storage of EU personal data to remain within the EU for primary model inference and logs. We also need to understand any edge or control-plane components that may operate outside the EU and whether any customer data (including telemetry) could transit or be stored outside the EU.

Specific asks (short list):
- Which Redwood components (control plane, metrics, logging, model artifacts, KV cache, inference runtime) can be deployed in an EU region for hosted and dedicated deployments?
- Do any background services (telemetry/analytics, billing, model-ops orchestration) default to non-EU regions? Are there options to opt out or route them to EU-only endpoints?
- How does Redwood handle key management for customer-controlled encryption keys (bring-your-own-KMS) across AWS/GCP/Azure? Any known constraints?
- For customers who require strict geofencing, where do you place ephemeral edge nodes (APAC, US) that are allowed to do caching, and what data is cached? Is cached data persisted or truncated after inference?
- Any exceptions for third-party integrations (DocuSign, cloud marketplaces) that require transfers? How are those documented?

Please provide a concise inventory + any operational exceptions. If easier, a short call later this week works.

Best,
Emma
Emma Collins
Senior Procurement Manager | Novamed Solutions

Emma / Novamed team — thanks for the RFI. Answers below are concise operational statements; I have attached a one-page residency matrix, our KMS integration guide, and the most recent SOC 2 report for your review. If you'd like, we can run a short 30-minute walkthrough on 2027-05-18 (calendar link below).

Executive summary:
- Redwood supports EU-only inference and storage for the primary inference path across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments. We run inference and persist inference outputs (generated text, embeddings) within the customer's selected EU region by default.
- Control plane services (account management, some non-essential analytics) are logically separable. For Hosted customers who require EU-only processing, we offer an EU control-plane partitioning option (enterprise-only) that keeps account-level metadata and telemetry in-region. For Dedicated and Private deployments, control-plane components run inside the customer's VPC or on-prem and do not egress EU data.
- Telemetry: Standard telemetry in Hosted mode is aggregated and delivered to Redwood analytics (default cluster in us-west) unless an EU-only telemetry agreement is in place. For enterprise contracts we provide: (a) EU-only telemetry endpoints; (b) data pseudonymization filters; or (c) a telemetry-forwarding connector so you retain telemetry in your environment.
- Key management & encryption: We support customer-managed keys (BYOK/CMEK) across AWS KMS, GCP KMS, and Azure Key Vault. For Hosted EU deployments we can integrate with customer KMS given cross-account roles and minimal IAM provisioning; for Dedicated we deploy a key forwarding proxy inside the VPC. Known caveat: HSM-backed keys requiring on-prem HSMs may need additional network configuration (we document this in the attached KMS guide).
- Edge caching and ephemeral nodes: Redwood operates ephemeral edge nodes for low-latency prefix caching in certain regions (APAC, US). These nodes may cache non-sensitive prefixes (model KV cache + tokenizer artifacts) for performance. We do not persist customer-generated PII or full inference logs on edge nodes. All cache entries have a TTL (default 10 minutes) and are evicted on node shutdown; we can shorten TTLs for EU-sensitive customers to <1 minute.
- Third-party exceptions: Integrations that invoke external vendors (DocuSign, marketplace billing connectors) may transfer minimal metadata to those vendors to complete a workflow. We document each integration in the attachments and provide contractual clauses for data processing addenda.

Attachments included:
- residency-matrix-20270515.xlsx (matrix mapping components by deployment mode + exceptions)
- kms-integration-guide.pdf (step-by-step for BYOK/CMEK across clouds)
- SOC2-report-2026.pdf (redacted operational controls)

Operational notes / exceptions (exceptions we flag to Novamed):
- Hosted (self-serve tier): default telemetry and billing pipelines are multi-region and may touch US endpoints — enterprise customers should elect the EU-control-plane option.
- Marketplace deployments (cloud marketplace images): marketplace billing records may be processed by the marketplace provider and are subject to their egress; we provide template clauses and can negotiate restricted flows.
- Latency-sensitive fallbacks: during cross-region failover we may temporarily route inference to a secondary region (same continent preferred) — we surface this in SLOs and provide failback windows in the SLA.

Next steps:
1) Please confirm whether Novamed wants the enterprise EU-control-plane partition and whether you need shortened cache TTLs (<1 minute).
2) If Novamed requires a dedicated KMS proxy deployment in your VPC, we will run a quick network checklist.
3) I can schedule a 30-minute call 2027-05-18 to walk the matrix.

Regards,
Vanessa Ortiz
Head of Solutions | Redwood Inference
Attachments: residency-matrix-20270515.xlsx, kms-integration-guide.pdf, SOC2-report-2026.pdf

Subject: Re: RFI: location-specific hosting dependencies and exceptions — follow-ups & invite

Emma — quick clarifications inline and calendar invite attached: 

1) Edge cache identifiers: we will not store any reversible customer identifiers on ephemeral edge nodes. Edge nodes may temporarily hold non-reversible session hashes (one-way salted hashes) used for routing and cache hits; these are not reversible to original user identifiers. For Novamed we can disable even salted-hash caching if preferred.

2) EU-control-plane: this is an enterprise-only configuration (needs contract addendum). It provisions a logical partition and EU-hosted analytics pipeline; no data is replicated to Redwood's US analytics in that mode. Backups/snapshots: model artifacts and inference outputs are not replicated outside the chosen EU region unless you explicitly enable cross-region replication for disaster recovery — we will not enable that without written approval.

3) Marketplace/DocuSign: we have standard DPA and marketplace addendum templates; I will send them in a follow-up and we can redline.

I have scheduled the 30-minute walkthrough for 2027-05-18 09:30 UTC. Calendar link: https://calendar.example.com/meetings/novamed-availability-20270518. Please let me know attendees.

Action items:
- Marcus: prepare network checklist for KMS proxy (I will send to Novamed if they confirm).
- Laura: prepare short note on telemetry pseudonymization options (1 pager).
- Sergio: confirm TTL controls and send a line we can add to contract appendix.

Thanks — looking forward to the call.

Cheers,
Vanessa
